history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: no web source documents any Hindu temple named "Chitmang Valley Temple". Chitmang Hill is a geographical hill feature located at Medu Awe (Medu Hawe) village in Rongara block, South Garo Hills - about 23-25 km from Baghmara town - with a Christian cross or "chisol" erected on the hilltop (documented in a 2019 YouTube video titled "Cross or Chisol on the Chitmang Hill in the South Garo Hills"). The Meghalaya Police district page lists "Chitmang (Kailash) hill top" among South Garo Hills' tourist spots, alongside caves and lakes. The CSV row appears to misclassify a hilltop viewpoint carrying a Christian cross as a Hindu temple - keep-or-drop decision needed. CSV town "Baghmara" is the nearest town, not the site's location: Medu Hawe village is 23 km from the district headquarters Baghmara (per Census/civic data) and its block HQ is Rongara.

name: Chitmang Hill (CSV row name: Chitmang Valley Temple)
town_description: Baghmara is the district headquarters of South Garo Hills, Meghalaya, on the Bangladesh border. Chitmang Hill lies at Medu Awe village in Rongara block, ~23-25 km from Baghmara town.
tradition: Not a Hindu temple - a hilltop geographical feature with a Christian cross/chisol; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Guwahati Airport is the usual gateway for South Garo Hills; Shillong Airport is farther.
travel.railway: No railway station nearby; nearest major station is Guwahati, Assam.
travel.road: Reach Baghmara by road from Tura/Guwahati, then travel ~23-25 km toward Rongara/Medu Hawe. Local 4x4 or bike advised on remote stretches.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April (dry season) for Garo Hills hill sites.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Natural hilltop - daylight visits; no published hours (verify locally). Note: coordinates are map-pin level for Chitmang Hill (Rongara) - verify on ground. Media: no reliable site-specific image found after genuine searching.
